agent: wave 13 agent D - the claims that rest on writers only
question: Four published claims that are thinner than they read, each one a field or a scale established from its writers with no reader ever looked for: CDiplomacyStatus +0x59 `changed`, the direction of `surrender_progress`, what `check_variable` creates on a miss and whether it survives a save, and what an unnamed regiment holds in CSubUnit +0x68. Plus CEffect +0x14, which was not even known to be live.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress
addresses.comment:
0xFCB80 to three `ret 4` at 0xFCB9F, 0xFCBB9 and 0xFCC53 - one function, every exit sharing the same frame and reached by a jump from inside. 82 instructions, read end to end; twelve int3 before, ten after. `this` in ECX, the out pointer the single stack argument, and `out` comes back in EAX so the caller can do `call; mov eax,[eax]`.

    if (this->government_in_exile (+0x95))  *out = 0
    elif (this->province_count (+0xD08) == 0) *out = 1000
    else { unity = national_unity (+0x10B8) * 1000 / 100000        ; i.e. /100, so 10..1000
           if (unity == 0) *out = 1000
           else *out = clamp(0xFCC60(this) * 1000 / unity, 0, 1000) }

**1000 means on the brink of surrender and 0 means untouched.** `0xFCC60` is the share of the country's own claimed, owned victory points that it does **not** control, in thousandths, so the numerator rises as territory is occupied; and because `national_unity` is the **divisor**, the answer also rises as unity falls. Three independent corroborations: the `province_count == 0` arm - no provinces left at all - answers the maximum; `CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed` reads the same pair of fields at 0x4B99FF as `owned - controlled >= 2 VP`, i.e. as a loss; and BlackICE's own `open_peace_negotiation` decision offers the Soviet Union peace on an ascending ladder of `surrender_progress = 72, 74, 76, 78, 80, 82, 84, 90, 95` paired with rising desperation, while `sacrifice_the_homeland` (scorched earth) unlocks at 0.25/0.15/0.05.

The only engine caller is `CSurrenderProgressTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F8210), which divides by ten, so the script scale is 0..100. The game's own Lua registration calls this function **`CCountry::GetSurrenderLevel`** (ghidra/bicelib_findings.json, recovered from the luabind registration object), which is the engine's name for it and the reason the reading is now `confirmed` rather than named off a keyword.

**One consequence for a mod:** when the claims list at +0xD10 holds no province the country owns, 0xFCC60's `+0xBE0 <= 0` arm answers 0, so `surrender_progress` is 0 however much has been lost. It is a measure of occupied **claimed** territory, not of territory in general.
addresses.revises: The recorded pseudocode had the fraction upside down - it read `v = national_unity * 1000 / 100000; v = v * 1000 / <0xFCC60's answer>`, putting unity in the numerator and 0xFCC60 in the denominator. The bytes do the opposite: 0xFCC60's answer is the numerator (`mov eax,[ebp-4]` at 0xFCC11, which is the out slot 0xFCC60 wrote) and `unity/100` is the divisor (`mov eax,esi` at 0xFCC29 before the divide, esi being the unity quotient). Everything the old entry concluded about direction followed from that inversion: it said 'the main arm rises with unity, which reads as how far from surrendering rather than how close', and with the fraction the right way up the main arm **falls** with unity. The same inverted text was carried into ghidra/bicelib_findings.json, which buildFindings generates, so fixing it here fixes both. FINDINGS-invasion.md's prose (line 281) had the arithmetic right all along - this is trap 14's fourth question with the answer the other way round from the 2026-10-05 case: the *entry* was wrong and the *prose summary* was right. Also added: the +0xD08 arm is a province count, not an unknown field, and the `unity == 0` short circuit shares the +0xD08 exit.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4FCB80..0x4FCC55 instruction by instruction. The divide order is fixed by two facts: `lea edi,[ebp-4]` at 0x4FCBBC makes [ebp-4] the out slot handed to 0x4FCC60, and the `__allmul`/`__alldiv` pair at 0x4FCC18/0x4FCC30 takes `[ebp-4]` as its first operand and `esi` (the unity quotient computed at 0x4FCBE9-0x4FCC0B) as its divisor. 0xB99AF0 is the multiply and 0xB99980 the divide, read off the 32-bit fast path in 0x4FCC60 itself, which does the same arithmetic as `imul eax,eax,0x3e8; cdq; idiv esi`. 0x186A0 = 100000 is a lazily initialised static at [0x1BEB878], which matches national_unity's recorded 1000..100000 range so `unity/100` runs 10..1000 and the normalisation is 'relative to full unity'. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: `[ebp-4]` not being the slot 0x4FCC60 writes (it is - 0x4FCC60 stores through EDI and nothing else writes that slot), or the mod reading the other way, e.g. a decision that offers peace at a *low* surrender_progress. The 58 uses in the mod were read: the three distinct ladders (72..95, 10..70, 0.05..0.5) all point the same way.

addresses.name: CCountry::GetOccupiedVictoryPointShare
addresses.comment:
**The occupied share of a country's own claimed victory points, in thousandths - and the whole of what `surrender_progress` measures.** 0x4FCC60 to three bare `ret` at 0x4FCCC9, 0x4FCCDE and 0x4FCCEA, 43 instructions read end to end, one int3 after. Receiver in EAX, the out pointer in EDI, no stack arguments, and `out` comes back in EAX.

    owned = this->claimed_victory_points_owned (+0xBE0)
    if (owned <= 0)  { *out = 0; return out }
    held = this->claimed_victory_points_controlled (+0xBE4)
    *out = 1000 - clamp(held * 1000 / owned, 0, 1000)

So 0 when it still controls everything it owns, 1000 when it controls none of it, and **0 when it owns nothing it claims** - which is the one arm that does not mean what the name suggests and is why a country with an empty `claims` list never registers any surrender progress at all. The ratio is computed on a 32-bit `imul`/`idiv` fast path when `held` fits in +-2,147,035 and through the 64-bit helpers 0xB99AF0/0xB99980 otherwise. The `jne` at 0x4FCC6D and its `or eax,-1` arm are dead: the `jle` above it already took every value <= 0.

Its only caller is CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress (0xFCB80) at 0x4FCBC1. Named for what it computes rather than for the keyword, because the keyword belongs to its caller.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x4FCC60 end to end. The two fields are identified by their only writers, both inside CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0): zeroed together with the rest of that function's counter block at 0x4E2305-0x4E2323, then accumulated at 0x4E3050-0x4E3076 over the province-id list at CCountry +0xD10 (recorded `claims`), `+0xBE0 += prov->victory_points (+0x34) * 1000` when `prov->owner.id (+0x330) == country->id (+0xCA8)` and `+0xBE4 += ...` when `prov->controller_id (+0x338) == country->id`. All three province offsets are already in the record. `image.functionStart` answers 0xE21E0 for all three sites and `retsBefore` is empty, so they are one function. The clamp is read off `mov eax,0x3e8` at 0x4FCCB9 (which then yields `1000-1000 = 0` through the `mov edx,eax; sub edx,eax` pair) and `xor eax,eax` at 0x4FCCCE. `findBytes` finds **no** .rdata reference to 0x4FCC60, so it is not a vftable slot and trap 4 does not apply. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a third writer of +0xBE0 or +0xBE4 on a CCountry - the whole-image scan for the disp32 finds six sites for +0xBE0 and nine for +0xBE4, and all but the four named here are on CGameState/CInGameIdler, which is trap 12 and is why the chain was taken through RebuildNeighbours rather than off the displacement.

addresses.name: CVariables::AddVariable
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall CVariables::AddVariable(CVariables* variables@EDI, Hoi3CString* name, int value)
addresses.comment:
**The create half of `check_variable`'s side effect - and of `set_variable`'s and `change_variable`'s. It really does create.** 0x476FB0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x476FFC, 24 instructions read end to end. The registry arrives in EDI, the name and the value on the stack, and the new object comes back in EAX.

It asks `operator new` for **0x20 bytes** and lays out a variable: the Hoi3CString at offset 0 (inline buffer zeroed, length +0x10 = 0, capacity +0x14 = 0xF - the SSO shape), then the value at **+0x1C** from its second argument, then `Hoi3CString::assign` from the name argument, then an insert through the registry's **slot 6** (`[[edi]+0x18]`, pushed the object twice). It never looks the name up first, so on its own it would overwrite an existing payload inside the tree and leak the earlier object - but no caller does that, because all of them look up first and call this only on a miss.

**Six call sites in five functions**, and they are the whole of how a script variable comes into existence:
  - `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F01D0) at 0x5F0237, with `(&this->name, 0)` - this is the `check_variable` side effect, and the trigger then answers `0 >= value`
  - `CSetVariableEffect` slot 11 (0x5AF7A0) at 0x5AF7FE - `set_variable` finds and updates `+0x1C` in place, and creates only when the name is new
  - `CChangeVariableEffect` slot 11 (0x5AF810) at 0x5AF874 and 0x5AF8C6 - `change_variable` reads, adds its own `+0x3C` and writes back, so on a name that does not exist it calls this twice: once to make it zero and once more, which then finds it and updates in place
  - `CSetVariableCommand` slot 6 (0x1532C0) at 0x553313 - the same find-or-create, as a `CCommand`
  - `CVariables::GetValue` (0x76F60) at 0x476F8E - the generic accessor, which **has no callers at all** in this build

`CVariables::LoadKey` (0x77080, slot 4 of the CPersistent vftable 0x11BD724) does not call this; it builds the identical 0x20 bytes inline and inserts them the same way, filling the value through `TokenToFixedPoint`. That is what fixes the layout, because the loader's object is the one a savegame's `name=value` pair becomes.

Slot 6 of CVariables' own vftable (0x11BD700) is `NameTree_Insert` (0x4D8A0), a folded template body in eight tables that therefore stays class-free; it reduces to `TernarySearchTreeInsert` (0x4DA70), whose key comparison runs through `tolower`. **So variable names are case-insensitive** - unlike `remove_brigade`, which memcmps.

**The created variable does not reach the save.** See 0x77000.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x476FB0 end to end; `image.functionStart(0x476FB0)` answers itself and it opens `push ebp; mov ebp,esp`. EDI is never written in the body, which is what makes it a register argument, and every one of the six call sites loads it the same way - `mov edi,[db->+0x16C[id]]; add edi,0x1ac` (0x5F01FD/0x5F0209 in the trigger, 0x5AF7D1/0x5AF7DD in the effect), or `mov edi,ecx` in CVariables::GetValue - i.e. the embedded CVariables at CCountry +0x1AC. `ret 8` accounts for both stack slots. The 0x20 is the `push 0x20` at 0x476FB4. `findRefs.py --callers 0x476FB0` reports exactly six direct calls (0x476F8E, 0x553313, 0x5AF7FE, 0x5AF874, 0x5AF8C6, 0x5F0237) and `--callers 0x476F60` reports zero, which is what makes GetValue dead. The two slot bodies are attributed by `vtable.py --holding`: 0x5AF7A0 is CSetVariableEffect slot 11 and 0x5AF810 CChangeVariableEffect slot 11, one table each, so no fold. The layout is confirmed twice independently of this body: CVariables::LoadKey writes the same four fields in the same order at 0x47709A-0x4770A7 then `mov [esi+0x1c],eax` from TokenToFixedPoint at 0x4770DE; and the save walker passes the object straight to `SaveWriteNamedFixed(Hoi3CString* key@EAX, ...)` at 0x477036, whose first parameter is already recorded as `Hoi3CString*`, which can only be true if the string is at offset 0. +0x1C is the same offset CVariableTrigger::Evaluate compares against its own threshold. `findBytes` finds no .rdata reference to 0x476FB0, so it is not a vftable slot. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a seventh caller, or one of the four live callers not testing the lookup first - each of them has the `test eax,eax; je <create>` immediately after the slot-1 call.

addresses.name: CVariables::SaveSubtree
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CVariables::SaveSubtree(CVariables* this, CSaveWriter* writer, CTernaryNode* node)
addresses.comment:
**Why a variable set to zero is not in the savegame.** 0x477000 to the single `ret 8` at 0x477058, 36 instructions read end to end. An in-order walk of the variable tree: recurse into `node->low (+8)`, write this node's payload, recurse into `node->equal (+0x10)`, then iterate `node->high (+0xC)` as a loop. That order is why the `variables={}` block comes out alphabetically.

The payload step is the point:

    v = node->element (+0)
    if (v != 0 && v->value (+0x1C) != 0)
        SaveWriteNamedFixed(v, writer, v->value)

The `test eax,eax; je` at 0x47702B is a **zero test on the value**, so a variable whose value is exactly zero is skipped. There is no 'absent means zero' distinction to lose, because `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate` treats a missing name as zero anyway - but it does mean the variable `check_variable` creates on a miss **is session-scoped and erases itself at the next save**, so the side effect cannot accumulate across a save/load and cannot be seen from outside the process.

Reached only from `CVariables::SaveContents` (0x77060), which is slot 2 of CVariables' CPersistent vftable 0x11BD724 and is the whole of `add ecx,-0x24; if (this->root) 0x77000(writer, root)`. The -0x24 is the second-base adjustment: CCountry holds the tree part at +0x1AC and the CPersistent part at +0x1D0, and CCountry::SaveContents does the matching `lea esi,[edi+0x1d0]` before writing key 0x411 `variables` at 0x4CFE2D.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x477000 end to end. The zero test is `mov eax,[eax+0x1c]; test eax,eax; je 0x47703b` at 0x477028-0x47702D, skipping the only call to SaveWriteNamedFixed. Corroborated by the save corpus, with a control: across **45 saves and 4,815 `variables={}` blocks, 754 distinct variable names appear and not one of them is ever `0.000`**, while the same parse finds plenty of negatives (`Allies_Axis_help=-1.000`, `chromite_MaxSells=-2.000`, `aluminium_MaxSells=-4.000`) - so the writer is not dropping non-positive values in general, it is dropping exactly zero, which is what the `test`/`je` says. The traversal order is confirmed against the node layout read out of TernarySearchTreeFind (0xA7E030) and TernarySearchTreeInsert (0x44DA70) - see the CTernaryNode field revisions in this fragment - and against the saves being in alphabetical order. ECX is `this` because CVariables::SaveContents reaches it with `add ecx,-0x24` and the body only forwards it (`mov ebx,ecx`, then `mov ecx,ebx` on each recursion); `ret 8` accounts for the two stack arguments, pushed node-then-writer so the writer is the first. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: one `0.000` anywhere in a `variables={}` block in the corpus, or a second caller of 0x477000 that bypasses the test.

addresses.name: CVariables::GetValue
addresses.signature: int* __thiscall CVariables::GetValue(CVariables* this, int* out, Hoi3CString* name)
addresses.comment:
**The generic read of a script variable, and it creates the variable it fails to find.** 0x476F60 to two `ret 8` at 0x476F81 and 0x476F9F, 21 instructions read end to end, eleven int3 before and fourteen after.

    v = this->slot1(name)                 ; GuiTypeTree_FindByString
    if (v) { *out = v->value (+0x1C); return out }
    CVariables::AddVariable(this@EDI, name, 0)
    *out = 0; return out

**It has no callers in this build** - `findRefs.py --callers` reports zero direct calls - so the create-on-read behaviour reaches the game only through `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate`, which does the same thing inline. It is worth recording anyway, because it is the clearest statement of the intended semantics: in this engine reading a variable is what brings it into existence, and the trigger is not doing anything unusual.
addresses.evidence: Read 0x476F60 end to end. `mov edi,ecx` at 0x476F68 is what makes `this` the EDI argument of AddVariable at 0x476F8E; `[ebp+8]` is the out pointer (written at 0x476F7C and 0x476F97) and `[ebp+0xC]` the name (esi, pushed to slot 1 at 0x476F6F and to AddVariable at 0x476F87). `mov eax,[edi]; mov edx,[eax+4]` is slot 1, which the record already names GuiTypeTree_FindByString, and `+0x1C` is the variable's value as read by CVariableTrigger::Evaluate. Both exits are `ret 8` and both leave the out pointer in EAX. Eleven int3 above 0x476F60 and the previous function's `ret 4` at 0x476F52, so the boundary is clean in both directions and trap 2 does not apply; `findBytes` finds no .rdata reference and `vtable.py --holding` reports no table. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a caller - or slot 1 of 0x11BD700 not being the find, which the recorded GuiTypeTree_FindByString entry settles.

struct_fields.name: changed
struct_fields.comment:
Set to 1 by everything that changes the pair's standing, and **read by nothing in the image**. The whole universe of `[reg+0x59]` instructions in `.text` is 60 sites - 52 stores, 7 loads and one `lea` - and every one of the eight non-stores belongs to another class: three to CCreateUnitCommand (vftable 0x11C36D4), three to the CSetRandomSeed/CPauseGame command family (vftable 0x11D3434), one to a refcounted SEH object at 0x8364B0, and the `lea` to a hash-padding buffer at 0xAF8D40. **Thirty-seven of the 52 stores are on a CDiplomacyStatus**, all reached as `country->diplomacy_status_array (+0xE28)[id]` or through one of two setter helpers whose first act is this write - 0xA4A400 (which also writes +0x4C and then, if `g_CCurrentGameState->in_game` is set, ORs 0x100 into something reached through the state's +0xBE8, i.e. refreshes the interface) and 0xA4A3B0 (which also frees the casus-belli list). So the interface refresh is done by the **writer**, not by a reader of this flag.

The writers are CCountry::ChangeRelation (both directions, 0x4E65D8 and 0x4E660B) and **six** of the nine CRelation::Activate bodies - CAlliance, CGuarantee, CNap and CDependency twice each, one side apiece for CCasusBelli and CInfluence - plus CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars, CCountry::AfterLoad, CCountryEventEffect::Execute, CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey's neighbourhood and several of the command LoadKeys.

Nothing reads it, so `changed` describes its writers and cannot be falsified beyond that; it is kept rather than renamed because no better name is available from a body that has no consumer.
struct_fields.revises: Two corrections to a comment that was honest about being thin. (1) It said 'seven of the nine CRelation::Activate bodies set it ... CNap, CGuarantee, CAlliance, CDependency, CCasusBelli, CInfluence and CTradeRoute. CAlign's and CEmbargo's do not.' **CTradeRoute::Activate does not set it either** - there is no `[reg+0x59]` instruction anywhere between 0xA4AB48 and 0xAF8DD0, so the complete whole-image census excludes its whole body, not just the part a bounded decode reaches. It is six of nine, and the three that do not are CAlign, CEmbargo and CTradeRoute. (2) It said 'No reader was looked for'. One has now been looked for, exhaustively, and there is none - and the writer count was eleven, which is a count of nothing in particular: 37 store sites on a CDiplomacyStatus across about eighteen functions, including two dedicated setters the old reading did not have. And the sub-question the record invited - why CAlign and CEmbargo differ - **has no answer, because its premise is wrong**: it is three bodies, not two, and neither of the two rules that could have separated them survives. Materialising g_CCurrentGameState does not (CAlliance, CNap, CCasusBelli and CInfluence all do it and all set the flag; CGuarantee and CDependency do neither); writing one direction against both does not (CEmbargo writes both and does not set it, CInfluence writes one and does). With no reader, the three omissions have no consequence either way.
struct_fields.evidence: A complete census rather than a scan: `.text` split on runs of int3 and each chunk decoded from its own start (trap 9, no linear sweep), collecting every instruction with a memory operand whose displacement is 0x59 and whose base is a register other than esp/ebp. 60 sites. **Positive control, and it is the strong form**: the same census finds every writer the record already names - 0x4E65D8 and 0x4E660B in CCountry::ChangeRelation, 0xA46DDF/0xA46E05 in CGuarantee::Activate (0xA46DB0, read end to end here: 30 instructions, `+0x59 = 1` then `+0x1C = this` on each side), 0xA47CB3 in CCasusBelli::Activate, and so on - so its silence about reads is a result. Three blind spots were closed separately: an indexed form `[reg+reg*n+0x59]` has three hits, all garbage decodes in chunks with no 0xE28 (`ror byte`, `fcomp`); a word or dword load spanning byte 0x59 has 34 hits at disp 0x58, all 32-bit pointer walks on other classes (CDiplomacyStatus +0x58 is a recorded uint8_t); and `movzx`/`cmp byte` at +0x59 is inside the census and produced none on a status. One census hit, `add byte ptr [edx+0x59], dl` at 0x4E608B, is a false positive from the jump table embedded in CDiplomaticAction::Create - `retsBefore(0x4E5800, 0x4E608B)` returns 25 `ret`s, which says so loudly. The nine Activate bodies were each decoded from their entries and counted. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: any read of +0x59 whose base register is a CDiplomacyStatus, or a CRelation::Activate body whose +0x59 write sits past a chunk boundary the census crossed - it decodes through abutting functions rather than stopping at them, so that direction is covered.

struct_fields.name: claimed_victory_points_owned
struct_fields.comment: **Victory points in thousandths, summed over the provinces in the `claims` list (+0xD10) that this country owns.** Written only by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0), which zeroes it with the rest of its counter block at 0x4E2305 and then accumulates `prov->victory_points (+0x34) * 1000` at 0x4E3059 for each claimed province whose `owner.id (+0x330)` is the country's own `id (+0xCA8)`. Two readers: CCountry::GetOccupiedVictoryPointShare (0xFCC60), which uses it as the denominator of the surrender measure, and CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed, which at 0x4B99FF takes `owned - controlled` and tests it against 0x7D0 (2 victory points) to decide an ally is losing real ground. Other classes also carry a field at +0xBE0 - CGameState and CInGameIdler both write one - so a bare displacement scan here is trap 12.
struct_fields.evidence: The whole-image disp32 scan finds six `[reg+0xBE0]` sites; the four on a CCountry are 0x4E230B and 0x4E3059 (both inside 0xE21E0 - `functionStart` agrees and `retsBefore` is empty), 0x4FCC63 and 0x4B9A05. 0x65A8AA is inside CInGameIdler::Enter and 0x67FEE8 inside CGameState::LoadKey, neither a CCountry. The thousandths are the `imul ecx,ecx,0x3e8` at 0x4E3053, and +0x34 is already recorded as `victory_points` on CProvince and CMapProvince, +0x330 as the id half of `owner` and +0xCA8 as `id`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the list at +0xD10 not being `claims` - the loop reads node->+0 as a province id and node->+8 as the next node, which is the node shape that field's record describes - or the accumulation being gated on something other than the owner test, which is the `cmp [eax+0x330], ecx; jne` at 0x4E3048.

struct_fields.name: claimed_victory_points_controlled
struct_fields.comment: **Victory points in thousandths, summed over the provinces in the `claims` list (+0xD10) that this country currently controls.** The other half of +0xBE0, written in the same loop in CCountry::RebuildNeighbours: zeroed at 0x4E2311 and accumulated at 0x4E3076 on `prov->controller_id (+0x338) == country->id`. `1000 - 1000 * controlled / owned` is the occupied share of the country's own territory, which is what `surrender_progress` is built from. CGameState also has a field at +0xBE4 and writes it with `movss`, i.e. as a float - a displacement scan mixes the two.
struct_fields.evidence: Nine `[reg+0xBE4]` sites in `.text`; the four on a CCountry are 0x4E2311, 0x4E3076, 0x4FCC74 and 0x4B99FF. The remaining five (0x67BB34, 0x67D6CB, 0x681156, 0x681171, 0x6811F0) are all `movss` on a CGameState. The owner/controller split is the two `cmp` against `country->id` at 0x4E3048 and 0x4E3065, and +0x338 is already recorded `controller_id`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the two accumulations being gated the same way, which would make 0xFCC60 always answer 0.

struct_fields.name: province_ids_end
struct_fields.comment: Tail of the province-id list whose head is `province_ids` at +0xD00, between it and `province_count` at +0xD08 - the usual head/tail/count triple. Read as the previous node and overwritten with the new one by the append at 0x4DD21E, and zeroed with the other two by CCountry::AfterLoad at 0x4D4AC8.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x4D4AC2-0x4D4ACE writes +0xD00, +0xD04 and +0xD08 with the same zero register in three consecutive instructions, which is the shape every other head/tail/count triple in the record has (CCountry +0xF24/+0xF28/+0xF2C, CDiplomacyStatus +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44). The append at 0x4DD215-0x4DD237 reads the count, stores the node into +0xD04, writes count+1, and on the first append also writes +0xD00. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: +0xD04 holding something other than a node pointer, which the append's `mov [esi+0xd04], eax` with eax the freshly allocated node rules out.

struct_fields.name: province_count
struct_fields.comment: **How many provinces the country holds** - the count of the list at +0xD00, and the field `CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress` tests against zero to answer the maximum. There is a one-instruction accessor for it at rva 0x1010C0 (`mov eax,[ecx+0xd08]; ret`), which is the shape of a registered Lua getter. Incremented by the append at 0x4DD224 and zeroed with the head and tail by CCountry::AfterLoad at 0x4D4ACE; 48 `[reg+0xD08]` sites exist in `.text` and most of the readers are in the AI module.
struct_fields.evidence: The triple at 0x4D4AC2-0x4D4ACE and the append at 0x4DD215-0x4DD237, as for +0xD04: `mov ecx,[esi+0xd08]; lea edx,[ecx+1]; mov [esi+0xd04],eax; mov [esi+0xd08],edx; test ecx,ecx; je <write the head>` is a count being incremented and tested for 'was the list empty'. The accessor at 0x4FCBA2's sibling 0x5010C0 is padded on both sides by nine int3 and is a single instruction plus `ret`. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the increment not being an increment, or +0xD00 not being a list - its own record describes walking it in CCountry::UpdateIC.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment:
**The regiment's own name, always present, and the only thing `remove_brigade` can ever match.** Saved as `name` inside a `regiment={}` block, and the loader puts it back. Across the 45-save corpus there are **788,880 regiment blocks and 788,880 of them carry a `name=`, none of it empty**, so an 'unnamed regiment' does not exist at runtime: 290,876 of those instances (7,133 distinct strings) hold an engine-generated name of the shape `<ordinal> <abbrev> Regiment` - `1st HQ Regiment`, `2nd Art Regiment`, `1st Wagon Regiment` - and the rest hold the historical name the order of battle gave them. A wing is a CSubUnit too and carries its name here in the same way.

**So `remove_brigade = <a subunit type>` can never match**, and nothing in the mod tries: of 6,132 distinct `remove_brigade` values none is one of the 1,427 subunit type tokens the mod's `units/*.txt` declare.
struct_fields.revises: The comment was 'historical regiment name, saved as `name`', which left open what a regiment the order of battle did not name holds here - the question FINDINGS-effects.md raises against CRemoveBrigadeEffect::Execute, and the one that decides whether a type token could ever match. It cannot: there is no such thing as a regiment without a name, because the engine generates one. The old reading rested on a decode of CSubUnit::SetType finding no write to +0x68, which is absence in one function and not absence; the savegame settles it positively instead. The type is also spelled out - the record had it as Hoi3CString already, which the save corroborates.
struct_fields.evidence: Every `regiment={}` block in the 45 saves under the mod's own save-games folder was parsed and its depth-1 `name=` collected (depth-1 so a nested block's name cannot be miscounted): 788,880 blocks, 788,880 names, 30,600 distinct, zero empty and zero missing. The generated shape was counted with the regex `^\d+(st|nd|rd|th) [A-Za-z-]+ Regiment$`. The type-token test collected every `^\s*([a-z0-9_]+)\s*=\s*\{` key in `units/*.txt` (1,427) and intersected it with the 6,132 distinct remove_brigade values: empty. Both sides were read as cp1252, per CLAUDE.md. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: one regiment block in any save with no `name=` or with `name=""`, or a remove_brigade value that is a type token.

struct_fields.name: unused
struct_fields.comment:
**A byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image.** The family's base constructor is inlined everywhere it is used and writes, in this order, `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` (the CList base), `byte +0x14 = 0`, `token (+4) = 0x18D`, `word +0x1C = 0` (the `use_this`/`use_from` pair as one word), then the concrete class's vftable. CEffect::LoadKey (0x599CA0) does that 41 times, once per switch case, and three out-of-line constructors do it with the zero in a register (0x99E277, 0x9A26EE, 0x9AFF0D). There is no other write and **no read at all**, byte-sized or otherwise, in any of the 247 slot bodies the 109 `*Effect` vftables hold.

It is a declared member rather than padding - `+0x14` is a byte with three bytes of slack before `keyword` at +0x18, exactly as `+0x1C`/`+0x1D` have two before +0x20 - but it is dead in this build, so the name says only that.

**This corrects the record's prose, not an earlier field record** - there was none. FINDINGS-effects.md's open list and fragments/merged/effects.json's `slots_noted` both say 'CEffect +0x14 is left unnamed: nothing in the three destructors or in CEffect::LoadKey touches it.' CEffect::LoadKey is where it is written, 41 times, the first at 0x999D35, and the width was unknown: it is a byte, not a dword. The destructors half of that claim stands - CEffect::~CEffect (0x59C540) zeroes exactly +0x8, +0xC and +0x10 at 0x99C596-0x99C59B, which is also what proves the CList base is three dwords and that +0x14 is CEffect's own rather than a fourth word of the list.
struct_fields.evidence: No field was recorded at this offset, so this is a new record and not a revision; what it revises is the prose quoted in the comment. The chain, not the displacement (trap 12): the 247 distinct slot bodies held by the 109 RTTI classes whose name ends in `Effect` were each decoded from the slot address - an entry by definition, so trap 2 cannot bite - and every byte-sized `[reg+0x14]` collected. 44 sites, 41 of them `..., 0` inside 0x599CA0 and the other three the same initialisation with the zero in al/cl/bl; **no byte read anywhere**. **Positive control, same bodies, same scan**: asked for +0x1C it returns 51 sites including `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x1c], 1` in body 0x59CB50 and `mov byte ptr [esi+0x1c], 1` in body 0x59D4A0 - precisely the two writers of `use_this` the record names - and a dozen readers of the `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x1c], 0` shape; asked for +0x18 as a dword it returns the single recorded writer at 0x59B630 (CEffect::LoadKey's common tail) and the recorded slot-6 reader at 0x416000. So the method sees both writers and readers of the live bytes either side of this one. A whole-image version of the scan was tried and discarded: +0x14 with +0x18 or +0x1C in the same register matches 478 sites, nearly all of them Hoi3CString capacity initialisations (`mov dword ptr [ecx+0x14], 0xf`), which is trap 12 and why the vftable chain is the right filter. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a reader outside the family's slot bodies - CEffect::GetBlockText and the event-option dispatcher at 0x5BF3D0 are the two places to look, and neither is a slot body, so this negative is bounded to the family's own virtuals.

struct_fields.name: element
struct_fields.comment: The CFlag, CVariable or CGuiType whose name ends at this node, or 0 where no name ends here. TernarySearchTreeFind returns `*(*slot)` from here on a match (0xA7E079) and TernarySearchTreeInsert writes it last (0x44DAFB), overwriting it on a key already present. A variable object has its Hoi3CString at offset 0, which is why CVariables::SaveSubtree can hand this pointer straight to `SaveWriteNamedFixed(Hoi3CString* key@EAX, ...)`.
struct_fields.revises: The type was `undefined4`, which decompiles every use of the payload as an anonymous dword. It is a pointer; the comment is otherwise unchanged.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x44DA9B writes 0 into +0 on a fresh node and 0x44DAFB/0x44DB14 write the caller's `value` argument there; 0xA7E07B dereferences it. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a use of +0 as a scalar.

struct_fields.name: low
struct_fields.comment: **The subtree for keys whose current character sorts below this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) - node->character < 0`: `lea esi,[edi+8]` in TernarySearchTreeFind (0xA7E068) and `lea ebx,[esi+8]` in TernarySearchTreeInsert (0x44DAF3), in both cases without advancing the key position. CVariables::SaveSubtree recurses into it **first**, which is why the savegame's `variables={}` block comes out alphabetically.
struct_fields.revises: It was `parent`, 'where a name added later hangs' - a name taken from BiceLib/GameClasses/CFlags.hpp, whose own comment admits 'what the tree means by each link has not been worked out'. It is the low child. The answer was already in the record: TernarySearchTreeFind's entry states the layout as `{void* value; char key; Node* low; Node* high; Node* equal;}` at +0, +4, +8, +0xC, +0x10 - so this is the two halves of the fact base disagreeing, with the function comment right and the header-sourced struct wrong (trap 14). It is not a small distinction: a traversal that recursed into a parent could not terminate, and CVariables::SaveSubtree recurses into +8 from the root.
struct_fields.evidence: Read both halves of the tree end to end. In the find (0xA7E030, 25 instructions) `sub eax,ecx` compares the folded key byte with `[edi+4]`; `jne` goes to `lea esi,[edi+0xc]` and then `test eax,eax; jg` keeps +0xC for a positive difference and falls to `lea esi,[edi+8]` for a negative one. The insert (0x44DA70, 44 instructions) mirrors it exactly at 0x44DAEA-0x44DAF6, and a fresh node has all three links zeroed at 0x44DAAE-0x44DAB4 with the node 0x14 bytes from `push 0x14`. The third witness is the output: CVariables::SaveSubtree walks low, payload, equal, then iterates high, and every `variables={}` block in all 45 saves is in alphabetical order. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the sign test going the other way, which would make the save come out reversed.

struct_fields.name: high
struct_fields.comment: **The subtree for keys whose current character sorts above this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) - node->character > 0` (0xA7E061 in the find, 0x44DAEE in the insert), again without advancing the key. CVariables::SaveSubtree iterates it as the loop's continuation rather than recursing, which is the last leg of the in-order walk.
struct_fields.revises: It was `sibling`, with no comment beyond the word - the same CFlags.hpp guess as +0x8. It is the high child, as TernarySearchTreeFind's own entry already said.
struct_fields.evidence: The `jg 0xa7e06b` at 0xA7E066 keeps `lea esi,[edi+0xc]` for a positive difference; the insert's `jle 0x44daf3` at 0x44DAEC does the same. CVariables::SaveSubtree's `mov esi,[esi+0xc]; test esi,esi; jne` at 0x47704B closes its loop on it. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the find descending +0xC on a negative difference.

struct_fields.name: equal
struct_fields.comment: **The next character of a key that matched this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) == node->character` and the key has more to go, together with `key++` - `inc ebx; lea esi,[edi+0x10]` in the find (0xA7E05B) and `inc edi; lea ebx,[esi+0x10]` in the insert (0x44DAE4). Where the key ends instead, the node's `element` is the answer. **Both ends of the tree fold the key byte through `tolower` (0xB96692) and store the folded form, so every lookup in this structure is case-insensitive** - which is already recorded on TernarySearchTreeFind and is what makes `check_variable = { which = BaseIC }` and `which = baseic` the same variable, in contrast to `remove_brigade`, which memcmps a name.
struct_fields.revises: It was `child`, with no comment - the third CFlags.hpp guess. It is the equal child, as TernarySearchTreeFind's own entry already said, and naming it is what makes the structure readable: `low`/`high` are the binary search within one character position and `equal` is the only link that advances the key.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA7E054's `jne` falls through on a zero difference to `cmp byte ptr [ebx+1], al` (al is 0 there, so this is the end-of-string test) and then to `inc ebx; lea esi,[edi+0x10]`; the insert does the same at 0x44DADD-0x44DAE5. The `tolower` call is at 0xA7E046 in the find and 0x44DAA1/0x44DACF in the insert, and only the insert's result is stored (`mov [esi+4], al` at 0x44DAA9), which is why the comparison needs no second fold. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: the key position advancing on a low or high descent, which would make the structure a plain BST over whole strings.

slots_noted: No vftable slot is named here on purpose. 0x77060 (CVariables::SaveContents) and 0x77080 (CVariables::LoadKey) are slots 2 and 4 of CVariables' CPersistent vftable 0x11BD724 and are described inside 0x77000's and 0x76FB0's comments instead of recorded, because CVariables carries two vftables - the tree one at CCountry +0x1AC (0x11BD700) and the CPersistent one at +0x1D0 (0x11BD724) - and project.json's vftable_slots is keyed by class with no way to say which table a slot number belongs to. Both are on the frontier. Slot 6 of 0x11BD700 is NameTree_Insert (0x4D8A0), already recorded class-free because the body sits in eight tables (trap 4), and it must not be named for CVariables. 0xFCC60, 0x76FB0 and 0x77000 are not in any vftable: findBytes over .rdata finds no reference to any of the three.
